bin/subfleet's alias loop enumerates every CARPOOL_<NAME> in the environment and exports SUBFLEET_<NAME> with the same value before exec'ing the CLI, so CARPOOL_STATE_DIR becomes SUBFLEET_STATE_DIR and the entire status snapshot is read from /private/tmp/iso-state (paths.state_dir(), paths.py:48).

Mirror of the previous divergence: the shell skips an empty legacy value (`[ -z "${!_legacy:-}" ]`), while Python has no emptiness test and copies "" into SUBFLEET_STATE_DIR. Under the Python-only path an empty CARPOOL_STATE_DIR therefore manufactures an empty SUBFLEET_STATE_DIR; paths._env_path then decides what an empty override means.

The shell copy tests `-n`, so an EMPTY SUBFLEET_STATE_DIR does not count as set and is overwritten by CARPOOL_STATE_DIR; the Python copy tests `new not in os.environ` (__init__.py:33), so the empty string counts as set and CARPOOL_STATE_DIR is dropped. Through bin/subfleet the shell runs first and wins; through `python3 -m subfleet.cli` (what bin/subfleet-watch:9 execs, with no alias loop) only the Python rule applies.
Two specifically-named legacy variables outside the CARPOOL_ prefix are renamed too: CLAUDE_LANE_CARPOOL -> CLAUDE_LANE_SUBFLEET and DELEGATE_CARPOOL -> DELEGATE_SUBFLEET.
